BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

Of course. Here is my detailed review of the Seller's documents against the Wattlebridge Holdings negotiation playbook for Project Kestrel.

### Executive Summary

The Seller's draft represents a significant departure from the agreed baseline and our internal playbook in almost every material area. Their positions are heavily skewed towards limiting their liability and shifting risk to the Buyer, effectively gutting the warranty protection we require. The approach is to use broad, boilerplate limitations that override specific, critical protections. Our pushback must be firm, prioritising the protection of fundamental risks (title, fraud, key customer/finance issues) over the general warranty cap, which is a secondary negotiating point.

---

### Detailed Analysis of Departures from the Playbook

#### 1. General Warranty Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)
*   **Seller's Position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
*   **Playbook Position:** Starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% cap is a **conditional fallback** requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost.
*   **Departure:** The Seller has unilaterally adopted the conditional fallback without authority.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back to the 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position.** If Amelia Frost is prepared to authorise the 20% cap, this becomes a secondary concession. The Seller's justification for "administrative simplicity" is weak and does not warrant such a significant reduction in our protection.

#### 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)
*   **Seller's Position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; Basket of AUD 250,000 with **only the excess above the basket recoverable**.
*   **Playbook Position:** De minimis AUD 5,000; Aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with **seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded**.
*   **Departure:** The Seller has dramatically increased both thresholds and, critically, introduced a "first-dollar" basket (excess only), which is the most Buyer-unfriendly structure. This means we cannot recover a AUD 100,000 claim at all, as it falls below the basket, and a AUD 300,000 claim only yields AUD 50,000.
*   **Recommendation:** **Firmly reject this structure.** Insist on our playbook position: a low de minimis (AUD 5,000) and a low basket (AUD 50,000) with first-dollar liability once the basket is exceeded. This is a non-negotiable point for meaningful warranty protection.

#### 3. Time Limits (Clause 12.3 / 13)
*   **Seller's Position:** 18 months for general warranties. Proposal that this applies to **all Claims** unless stated otherwise.
*   **Playbook Position:** 24 months for general warranties (18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's approval). Fundamental/Title claims must have a separate, longer regime (at least six years).
*   **Departure:** The Seller has set the fallback time limit without approval and, more importantly, attempts to apply it universally, which would severely restrict claims for fundamental matters like title and capacity.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject the universal application.** Insist on the 24-month general period (or seek Amelia's approval for 18 months as a concession). More critically, **strongly object to the conflation of regimes.** We must establish a separate, robust regime for Fundamental/Title claims with a 100% cap and a minimum six-year term, outside the general basket and de minimis.

#### 4. Limitations & Reliance (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
*   **Seller's Position:** Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
*   **Playbook Position:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be **carved out** of all caps, baskets, time limits, and exclusive remedies to the maximum extent enforceable.
*   **Departure:** This is a critical and dangerous departure. The Seller's wording attempts to insulate themselves from the consequences of their own fraud or deliberate misconduct by subjecting those claims to the same restrictive caps and time bars.
*   **Recommendation:** **This is a major red line.** We must insist on explicit carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct. No exceptions. This is a standard market protection and essential for our risk management.

#### 5. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2])
*   **Seller's Position:** Relies on "general disclosure of the data room and public registers."
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to use a broad, deemed-disclosure clause. This means any Buyer claim could be defeated by the Seller pointing to some document in the data room, even if it was not specifically brought to our attention. This negates the purpose of specific warranties.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject the deemed disclosure concept.** Insist that disclosure must be "fair and specific" and that the Seller's knowledge (of key individuals) is the relevant standard. The data room is a source of information, not a shield against claims for matters not specifically disclosed.

#### 6. Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3)
*   **Seller's Position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers **had knowledge**, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
*   **Playbook Position:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
*   **Departure:** The Seller has introduced an extremely broad knowledge exclusion that would effectively void warranties for any matter our due diligence team *could have* discovered. This is unacceptable.
*   **Recommendation:** **Demand deletion of this clause.** If a knowledge qualifier is unavoidable, it must be limited to the actual knowledge of **specific named individuals** on the Seller's side, after reasonable enquiry, and must not apply to title, capacity, fraud, or the specific indemnities (e.g., Ironquay).

#### 7. Bluefen Consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3 / Disclosure Letter [2])
*   **Seller's Position:** Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is proposing a weak "reasonable endeavours" obligation and a "consent-on-delivery" structure. This leaves the Buyer with the risk that the consent is delivered at the last minute but is ineffective because its pre-conditions are not met.
*   **Recommendation:** **Insist on a strong, conditional obligation.** The Seller must use their best efforts to obtain the consent *and* provide evidence that all conditions in the consent have been satisfied *prior to Completion*. The consent itself must be legally effective. This is non-negotiable given Bluefen's ~30% revenue significance.

#### 8. Riverlark Facility (Clauses 2 / 7 / Disclosure Letter [3])
*   **Seller's Position:** Release to be provided **following Completion**.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is pushing all risk and timing onto the post-completion period. A AUD 3.2M debt with change-control rights is a critical liability that must be cleared at or before Completion.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-completion release.** Require the debt to be repaid in full from the Completion funds, with all security released simultaneously. If a post-completion structure is absolutely necessary, it requires an irrevocable undertaking from the Seller and **prior written approval from Amelia Frost**.

#### 9. Employee Bonuses (Funds Flow / Disclosure Letter [5])
*   **Seller's Position:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
*   **Playbook Position:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to exclude these liabilities from the completion mechanics, leaving the Buyer potentially responsible for them post-completion or creating an undisclosed liability.
*   **Recommendation:** **Insist these be treated as a Seller liability.** They must be explicitly itemised in the funds flow as a deduction from the purchase price (i.e., the Seller funds them) or carved out as a pre-Completion obligation of the Seller. The on-costs (payroll tax, super) must also be identified and covered.

#### 10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure Letter [4])
*   **Seller's Position:** Indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
*   **Playbook Position:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is refusing to broaden the indemnity, which is necessary to cover potential broader IP infringement claims beyond just the SOW3 payment.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push for a broader indemnity** that covers any claims arising from the use of the Ironquay materials, not just the specific payment. We should also note that the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified and the indemnity must cover the full potential liability.

#### 11. Export/Privacy Incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure Letter [6])
*   **Seller's Position:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
*   **Playbook Position:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to downplay the issue and potentially limit their reporting obligations.
*   **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the characterisation.** We must preserve our right to full information. Insist on ongoing reporting and investigation obligations on the Seller, and ensure the warranty schedule accurately reflects the *potential* for a breach and associated liabilities, without the Seller prematurely declaring it immaterial.

#### 12. Sandbar Renewals (Disclosure Letter [8])
*   **Seller's Position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
*   **Playbook Position:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
*   **Departure:** Minimal departure, but the Seller's classification is overly simplistic.
*   **Recommendation:** **Treat as a point for due diligence assessment.** We need to confirm independently whether these renewals are indeed ordinary-course, unavoidable, and not a form of disguised debt or a liability that should be settled pre-Completion. The "assess" position is maintained.

#### 13. Title (Disclosure Letter [10])
*   **Seller's Position:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is relying on an internal document as proof, which is insufficient.
*   **Recommendation:** **Insist on independent evidence.** This means we require a title report from our own lawyers, confirming good title, absence of encumbrances, and the Seller's corporate authority to sell. The share register is a starting point, not conclusive proof.

---

### Summary of Recommendations

1.  **Prioritise Fundamental Protections:** The most critical fights are the **fraud carve-out**, the **separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims**, and the **specific, conditional treatment of the Bluefen and Riverlark issues**. These protect us from catastrophic, unquantifiable risks.
2.  **Reject Boilerplate Overrides:** Firmly oppose any attempt to apply general limitations (caps, time bars) to all claims. The Seller's draft is structured to do exactly this.
3.  **Reform the Warranty Regime:** The proposed thresholds (AUD 25k/250k excess-only) are unacceptable. We must hold the line for our playbook position (AUD 5k/50k first-dollar) to ensure the warranties provide real protection.
4.  **Control Disclosure and Knowledge:** Reject deemed disclosure and broad buyer-knowledge exclusions. These clauses would render the warranties meaningless.
5.  **Escalate Conditional Points:** The 20% warranty cap and 18-month general claims period are only acceptable with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost**. We should not concede these without that approval.
6.  **Itemise Specific Liabilities:** Ensure all known liabilities (employee bonuses, Ironquay, export incident) are explicitly addressed in the SPA and funds flow, leaving no room for the Seller to argue they are excluded by the general terms.

In short, the Seller's draft is a non-starter in its current form. We need to systematically walk back each position to our agreed playbook, with the highest priority on protecting against fundamental and known material risks.

### Summary of Recommendations

1.  **Prioritise Fundamental Protections:** The most critical fights are the **fraud carve-out**, the **separate regime for Fundamental/Title claims**, and the **specific, conditional treatment of the Bluefen and Riverlark issues**. These protect us from catastrophic, unquantifiable risks.
2.  **Reject Boilerplate Overrides:** Firmly oppose any attempt to apply general limitations (caps, time bars) to all claims. The Seller's draft is structured to do exactly this.
3.  **Reform the Warranty Regime:** The proposed thresholds (AUD 25k/250k excess-only) are unacceptable. We must hold the line for our playbook position (AUD 5k/50k first-dollar) to ensure the warranties provide real protection.
4.  **Control Disclosure and Knowledge:** Reject deemed disclosure and broad buyer-knowledge exclusions. These clauses would render the warranties meaningless.
5.  **Escalate Conditional Points:** The 20% warranty cap and 18-month general claims period are only acceptable with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost**. We should not concede these without that approval.
6.  **Itemise Specific Liabilities:** Ensure all known liabilities (employee bonuses, Ironquay, export incident) are explicitly addressed in the SPA and funds flow, leaving no room for the Seller to argue they are excluded by the general terms.

In short, the Seller's draft is a non-starter in its current form. We need to systematically walk back each position to our agreed playbook, with the highest priority on protecting against fundamental and known material risks.
